newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris okay $2 bln Amoco led Caspian oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Azeris okay $2 bln Amoco led Caspian oil deal.

text.p: Azerbaijan's parliament ratified on Tuesday a $2 billion planned deal with a group of foreign oil companies, led by a unit of Amoco Corp of the United States, to tap the Dan Ulduzu and Ashrafi oil fields in the Caspian Sea.
Eighty-seven deputies voted in favour, and four against the deal, which is Azerbaijan's fourth major multi-billion dollar contract with foreign oil firms.
The production-sharing agreement will last 25 years, the first three years of which would involve exploration on an area covering 453 sq km.
Azerbaijan is to receive a one-off signing bonus of $75 million under the agreement, which was first initialled in December 1996.

The foreign partners in the deal are Amoco North Apsheron Ltd (30 percent), Unocal International Exploration of the United States (25.5 percent), Itochu Oil Exploration (Caspian Inc) of Japan (20 percent), and Delta Nimir of Saudi Arabia (4.5 percent).
Azerbaijan state oil company SOCAR holds a 20 percent stake in the deal.
Dan Ulduzu and Ashrafi are situated close to a third Azeri sector Caspian field under development, Karabakh.
SOCAR officials say the three fields are each estimated to contain reserves of 60 million tonnes of oil and 30 billion cubic metres of gas.
SOCAR said it had the right to include development of the Karabakh field into the agreement to tap Dan Ulduzu and Ashrafi if it was deemed commercially viable.
